x: Our greatest enigma however was not at his best and when Mick Firth of S.L.H. swept past him without even a challenge we wondered what would happen.

When Bill Kerr passed Mick Firth of S.L.H. to take us up to 5th place we knew that the form he had shown in our road race two weeks earlier was no flash in the pan and our confidence in entrusting him with this crucial leg was justified.

He was forced to give away a place to Mick Firth of S.L.H. who ran second fastest on this particular stage. At the end of this leg we were nearly five minutes adrift - the leaders at this point being Bristol with Derby second and Portsmouth 3rd.
He had the unenviable task of trailing Mick Firth on this windswept stage and it was only towards the end of the leg that Firth's greater experience and fitness took him away from Cyril.

It was a very moving service, with readings from Gordon's book ''Running Wild'' and addresses given by Mick Firth and Chris Brasher. Looking back to Gordon's heyday in the late 1950s we can see now what an amazing influence he had on athletics in Britain.
